reviews.text:
I went there in the middle of the night for an emergency, and they did everything they could for me.
Their response and explanations were polite and I would recommend them.

I was assigned to this hospital to help with blood donation, so I made an appointment for a blood type test and went there. I was told to come by 5:30 because the explanation and test would take an hour (they close at 6:30), so I arrived 15 minutes early and filled out a questionnaire. From there, I was made to wait for an hour without any explanation, and when the doctor finally came, he didn't apologize and only asked if I wanted to be a donor or just donate to a friend's dog. I had lost my enthusiasm, so I told him the latter, and he said he would leave a one-page explanation about donating for reference, took my dog ​​away, and said that a nurse would return him in a few minutes, without explaining how long the test would take. After waiting for another 30 minutes or more, the doctor finally came and tried to talk about the test results and the future schedule, so I asked for an explanation about blood donation, and he just pointed to the explanation that had been left earlier and said it was as written there. It was so pathetic that he didn't even start calculating how many liters of blood I would need to donate until I asked. My dog ​​was bored and exhausted and slept soundly when we got home. I was worried because I don't know when my dog ​​might need your help, but I'm writing this assuming I'll be identified because I want you to improve your treatment of donor dogs. As I'm writing this, I've started to wonder if you intentionally treat them carelessly and sloppily, even though you have posters in the waiting room looking for donor dogs, so that anxious owners can easily decline.

From Suginami Dog and Cat Hospital to being under the Aeon umbrella, we have been under their care for 15 years, spanning two generations, for approximately 200 days. Our initial visit was for an oncology consultation, and they provided clear explanations and diagnoses, patiently working with us until we were completely satisfied. From long-serving doctors to younger veterinarians, they are all trustworthy.

The doctors in oncology, advanced medicine, orthopedics, dermatology, and dentistry are highly experienced not only in their respective specialties but also in general practice. They also coordinate effectively among doctors when there are issues outside their specialty or multiple symptoms, making it a hospital we can entrust our family's health to.

While the medical fees used to be a bit high, in recent years, based on the treatments we've received, that hasn't felt the case. Nighttime consultations have also resumed, and I feel that we can receive almost all the advanced medical care we need at this hospital. (MRI and CT scans are performed at an external facility.)

While there are many large, well-equipped animal hospitals these days, I can confidently say, based on my 15 years of experience, that this hospital is exceptional. From the skills and collaboration of the doctors to the customer service and accounting staff, they treat pets with genuine care and compassion, truly caring for those suffering from illness.

I believe that without mutual trust between the doctor and the patient/pet owner, evaluations become meaningless. I can confidently say that the seven specialists I received care from, in particular, are truly trustworthy doctors worthy of entrusting my family's lives to. I am overwhelmed with gratitude.

Although there are many animal hospitals in my neighborhood, I continued to go to this one, even though it took over 30 minutes by car. Even for minor symptoms, having a trustworthy doctor examine your pet provides peace of mind, and ultimately, it's the dogs and cats who suffer if the owner doesn't make the right judgment and evaluation…
The level wasn't high, there was no coordination, and there won't be a return visit.

I requested a spaying surgery. I was forced to undergo ridiculously expensive pre-operative tests, and although there were no abnormalities before the surgery, the post-operative recovery was not good, and despite numerous tests, the cause remained unknown. They insisted that if even one abnormality was detected, additional tests were necessary to determine the cause. Honestly, it felt like I was dealing with a veterinary student who knew nothing. It seemed like they couldn't make a simple diagnosis or judgment without test results because they lacked the necessary knowledge, and that's why they kept ordering tests. I will never take my dog ​​there again.

I had my dog ​​neutered here, but they said they couldn't perform the surgery without blood tests and X-rays, which cost over 60,000 yen.

I asked some acquaintances, and they said they'd never heard of a veterinary clinic that did that before, so if you're considering neutering your dog, I recommend checking with another veterinary clinic first to avoid any problems.
They treat your dog with great care and consideration.

I use this hospital as a second opinion when my pet needs tests that aren't available at my regular hospital.

I don't use it as my main veterinarian because the treatment costs are higher than at my regular hospital, making it difficult for me to afford to go there on a daily basis.

There are many veterinarians on staff, but I make appointments based on their schedules, as I would like to see the same trustworthy doctor whenever possible.

Personally, I really trust the explanations my regular veterinarian gives me, the way he interacts with animals, the way he explains things to owners, and the way he responds to our questions, so I would definitely use him again if I were to visit again.

Even though the doctor is great, there are two main reasons (excluding financial reasons) why I don't use this hospital as my main veterinarian (this is because it takes a long time from check-in to check-out. (It takes at least three times as long as at my regular hospital.)

With multiple departments and many doctors, there are a lot of patients, and I think it's unavoidable that appointments can take longer depending on the symptoms.
However, even though they operate by appointment, I wonder if it's appropriate to make them wait more than 30 minutes after the scheduled time without any explanation.

I don't want to cause my cat any more stress than necessary by locking him in a carrier for a long time at a hospital, which he doesn't like, so I definitely don't want to bring him there for vaccinations, checkups, or even if I'm just feeling a little anxious.

The second reason is because the staff's service is sloppy.

I sometimes call to make appointments or to consult with the doctor about his symptoms,

but there have been many times when the staff answered and said they would call me back, but never did, which made me distrust them.
Also, even when there were multiple people lined up at the reception desk, they prioritized chatting with someone who appeared to be a regular (small talk, not about animals) and kept those waiting for several minutes.
Also, when it was time to pay after the examination, I wasn't called for a while (I waited over 15 minutes even though the place was quiet), and when I asked how much longer it would take, they put me off even though they already had the paperwork in front of me. These negative impressions piled up, so I don't want to go there unless it's absolutely necessary.

I'm sure some regulars look forward to communicating with the staff, and I think it's great that they value communication. However, I wish they would prioritize their work over that.

Also, while I understand that this is unavoidable given the hospital's system, even simple procedures like nail clipping aren't performed in front of me, which personally concerns me as I can't see how the pets are held in place during the procedure.

I would rate my trust in the doctor as 5 stars,
but there are two main negative points that make it 3 stars.

Even though they offer late-night appointments, I contacted them right before closing time, but they still kindly listened to my concerns. I was hesitant about whether to wait and see or bring my dog ​​in, but I decided to go ahead with the appointment. Even though she was the last patient and needed treatment, the veterinarian and nurses welcomed us warmly, and thanks to their precise treatment, it was over in no time, leaving me with a great sense of relief. My dog ​​is usually very scared and trembles whenever I take her to the hospital after her spaying surgery at another clinic, but she seemed to relax thanks to the staff's kind treatment, even though it was her first time at this hospital. I was truly impressed by their wonderful service.

It's reassuring to know that such a veterinary hospital exists in our community. Thank you.

My kitten had a rare condition called congenital imperforate anus. His condition suddenly worsened and time was of the essence. I was desperate to get an appointment at a hospital that could perform surgery, and would have to wait for days, but the doctors and staff here saved me. The director of the clinic kindly explained the condition to me many times over the phone, and performed the surgery on the same day I took him in. I am filled with gratitude for all their efforts to save my little life.

This is a wonderful facility with many veterinarians on staff. 🟰 To cover their enormous expenses, they take advantage of pet owners' feelings and make them perform unnecessary tests.
This is a hospital that makes me wish they would put an end to this business that takes advantage of animals like dogs and cats.
Private animal hospitals are better.
The teachers are very kind and treat our pets like family, even calling us after we get home!
